question.text: In the F&O segment's order-driven market, how are orders matched on the exchange?

answer.text: Orders are timestamped and matched automatically on a price-time priority basis, with the best buy being the highest price and the best sell the lowest price
The broker manually chooses the counterparty for each order
Orders are matched only at month-end on a batch basis
Matching is restricted to institutional orders only

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes the F&O segment as an order-driven market where orders entered into the system are timestamped and matched automatically on a price-time priority basis. From the buy side, the best price is the highest available buy quote; from the sell side, the best price is the lowest available sell quote. Trading members must also execute client orders in a timely manner. The Trap: Manual selection of counterparties, batch-only matching, or institutional-only matching all conflict with the continuous automated, price-time matching described in the workbook. Note: Remember the matching rule: price-time priority, best buy = highest bid, best sell = lowest offer.
